text:
jamie (sre): SLO alert just fired for hosted-infer-us-midwest: p99 5xx jumped to ~4.8% over the last 10m, SLO burn starting. Multiple customers reporting timeouts/502s. tagging eng-sre + support
alerts-bot: ALERT: hosted-infer-us-midwest p99_5xx_rate > 1% for 10m (current 4.8%). Incident ID: INC-6398765300
maria (oncall): seeing same. dashboards? any deploys in last hour?
lee (observability): Grafana panels show a spike starting 2023-08-30T15:22:05Z, coincides with increased request rate from a few keys. Link: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/infra/hosted-infer-us-midwest?view=5xx
alex (support): Customer report from @AcmeCorp: "requests hang ~30s then 502. Repro curl attached." Their sample: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/infer -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-XXXX' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"gpt-mini-quant","input":"hello"}' -v```
sam (eng-runtime): quick check on gateway logs: increased 504s with backend 'prefetch-proxy' taking >25s then connection reset. Query I ran: ```kql=source:gateway AND region:us-midwest AND status>=500 AND timestamp>now-15m | stats count() by upstream, status_code``` results: prefetch-proxy 504: 1.2k, model-worker 502: 300
lee (observability): tracing gap noted — we have many gateway spans but only partial spans for prefetch-proxy at that time. Looks like span sampling dropped before the surge. Traces: https://trace.redwood/internal/trace/63987653xxxx
nora (cs): we have two high-velocity customers (AcmeCorp, BetaApps) actively hitting this window. BetaApps reports 5 minute outages on webhooks. They asked for ETA on fix.
ejamie (sre): possible hypothesis: prefetch cache eviction + concurrent cold KV loads causing long tail. Sam, any recent change to prefetch TTL or KV client?
sam (eng-runtime): rolled out prefetch-ttl bump for quant variants 15m->5m around 15:18 to reduce stale cache, rolled back for canary but looks like rollout continued to more nodes due to autoscaler bug. Reverting now.
lee (observability): adding queries to check client-side retries and prefix cache misses: ```logs| where upstream=="prefetch-proxy" and status==504 | parse "cache_miss=*" as miss | count by miss``` early run shows cache_miss=true ~85% of spike
alex (support): forwarding repro from customer with sample headers: X-Region: us-midwest, X-Client-Id: beta-77. They also saw elevated latency starting exactly after 15:18.
ejamie (sre): mitigation plan: 1) revert TTL change (sam) 2) enable temporary routing to dedicated-capacity pool for affected customer keys (ezra) 3) bump probe sampling to capture full traces (lee) 4) support: send short status to customers and ask for request ids
ezra (infra): can route beta-77 and acme keys to dedicated pool via routing rule set R-6398765300. Doing gradual shift now. ETA ~4m
sam (eng-runtime): TTL revert in progress, patch rolling — should finish in ~2m. Observability: recommend increasing span sampling to 100% for gateway->prefetch path for 30m.
lee (observability): ramping sampling, will post trace coverage once up. Also creating dashboard panel for prefix/KV hit ratio over 15m windows.
maria (oncall): good. after revert + routing, watch for p99 5xx to drop under 1% for 10m before closing.
jamie (sre): while rollback proceeds, add a temporary fallback policy at gateway to prefer smaller model-variant with lower KV pressure for keys showing >1% 5xx. Sam can enable canary fallback?
sam (eng-runtime): enabling fallback policy now for keys in R-6398765300. Posting command: ```rbctl set-route --keys beta-77,acme-90 --fallback=mini-serial --duration=30m```
lee (observability): initial metrics: 3m after actions p99_5xx -> 2.1%, prefetch 504 rate down 60%. Traces now show prefetch spans present.
ejamie (sre): good. keep monitoring. support, please update customers: short note with repro ids and actions taken.
alex (support): sending status update to customers: "We've routed your traffic to a dedicated pool and reverted a recent prefetch TTL change; engineers are monitoring. We'll follow up with a postmortem link."
nora (cs): pinged AcmeCorp + BetaApps with status and asked them to share any failing request IDs.
maria (oncall): logging runbook actions and timestamps for postmortem. if p99_5xx <1% and traces look healthy by 15:55, we can hand back to normal ops.
ejamie (sre): action items tracked: ACTION-6398765300 [sam] revert ttl, [ezra] route keys, [lee] increase sampling + dashboard, [alex] customer comms, [maria] record timeline. we'll reconvene if metrics regress.
lee (observability): note for postmortem: sampling policy allowed trace gaps during rate spikes — consider dynamic sampling tied to SLO alerts.
sam (eng-runtime): also adding safety guard to prevent prefetch-ttl rollouts during autoscaler events.
ajamie (sre): thanks everyone. closing thread for now, will reopen if alerts return. :thumbsup:
